<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; text-align: justify; margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0"><i>Defined Benefit Plan:</i> The Company provides for a gratuity obligation through a defined benefit retirement plan (the &#8220;Gratuity Plan&#8221;) covering eligible employees in India under Payments of Gratuity Act, 1972 till 20 November&#160;2025. On November&#160;21, 2025, the Government of India implemented four new labour codes&#8212;the Code on Wages, 2019, the Industrial Relations Code, 2020, the Code on Social Security, 2020, and the Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions Code, 2020&#8212;which consolidate 29 existing labour laws into a unified legislative framework.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; text-align: justify; margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0">The plan provides for a lump-sum payment to vested employees at retirement, death, incapacitation, or termination of employment, of an amount equivalent to 15 days (15 days / 26 days) of salary payable to the respective employee for each completed year of service, with a maximum limit prescribed per employee.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; text-align: justify; margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0">As of March&#160;31, 2026 and 2025, the entire gratuity plan of the Company was unfunded. The cost of providing benefits under this plan is determined based on an actuarial valuation at each year end. Actuarial valuation is carried out for gratuity using the projected unit credit method. These costs primarily represent the increase in the actuarial present value of the obligation for pension benefits based on employee service during the year and the interest on this obligation in respect of employee service in previous years. The obligation is included in &#8220;Accrued compensation and related benefits, current&#8221; while the long-term portion is included in &#8220;Other liabilities&#8221; on the consolidated balance sheets. Changes in fair value of the obligation are recorded in &#8220;Other comprehensive loss&#8221; in the consolidated statements of other comprehensive income/ (loss) and generally amortized over the average remaining service period of the active employees expected to receive benefits under the plan. According to ASC 715, changes to defined benefit plans, such as the Gratuity Plan in India, are accounted for as plan amendments, with the impact recognized in &#8220;Other comprehensive loss&#8221; at the amendment date.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; text-align: justify; margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0"><i>Compensated Absences:</i> The Company recognizes its liabilities for compensated absences dependent on whether the obligation is attributable to employee services already rendered, relates to rights that vest or accumulate and payment is probable and estimable. The obligation is included in &#8220;Accrued compensation and related benefits, current&#8221; while the long-term portion is included in &#8220;Other liabilities&#8221; on the consolidated balance sheets. In accordance with ASC 710, the impact of the new labour codes on compensated absences for employees in India in the consolidated statement of income for the year ended March&#160;31, 2026 was not significant. The Company&#8217;s total obligation with respect to compensated absences was $<span id="xdx_905_eus-gaap--CompensatedAbsencesLiability_iI_pn3n3_c20260331_ze2D1tSZBbWb" title="Compensated absences"><ix:nonFraction name="us-gaap:CompensatedAbsencesLiability" contextRef="AsOf2026-03-31" id="Fact001133" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="-3" scale="3" unitRef="USD">3,205</ix:nonFraction></span> and $<span id="xdx_902_eus-gaap--CompensatedAbsencesLiability_iI_pn3n3_c20250331_z4pEJFDzavSe" title="Compensated absences"><ix:nonFraction name="us-gaap:CompensatedAbsencesLiability" contextRef="AsOf2025-03-31" id="Fact001135" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="-3" scale="3" unitRef="USD">2,553</ix:nonFraction></span> for the years ended March&#160;31, 2026 and 2025, respectively.</p>

</ix:nonNumeric><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="From2025-04-01to2026-03-31" escape="true" id="Fact001137" name="us-gaap:EarningsPerSharePolicyTextBlock"><p id="xdx_844_eus-gaap--EarningsPerSharePolicyTextBlock_zWg5u0ffzFF4" style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; text-align: justify; margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0"><b><span id="xdx_86E_zLtA79dUglq2">Net Income / (Loss) per Share</span></b></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; text-align: justify; margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0">Basic net income / (loss) per share is computed by dividing income / (loss) available to ordinary shareholders by the weighted-average number of ordinary shares outstanding during the period. Diluted net income / (loss) per share is computed using the weighted-average number of ordinary shares and potential dilutive ordinary shares outstanding during the period. The Company has not considered the effect of the Warrants sold in its initial public offering (the &#8220;Initial Public Offering&#8221;) and private placement to purchase ordinary shares, and impact of FPA put option liability in the calculation of diluted net income / (loss) per share, since the instruments are not dilutive.</p>

As of March&#160;31, 2026 and 2025, these Series-A RPS held by the Company were classified as a held-to-maturity investment and recorded at amortized cost of $<span id="xdx_907_eus-gaap--AvailableForSaleDebtSecuritiesAmortizedCostBasis_iI_pn3n3_c20260331__us-gaap--StatementEquityComponentsAxis__custom--SeriesARedeemablePreferenceSecuritiesMember_zJYvK9AFjgPg" title="Held-to-maturity investments, amortized cost basis"><ix:nonFraction name="us-gaap:AvailableForSaleDebtSecuritiesAmortizedCostBasis" contextRef="AsOf2026-03-31_custom_SeriesARedeemablePreferenceSecuritiesMember" id="Fact001259" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="-3" scale="3" unitRef="USD">1,110</ix:nonFraction></span> and $<span id="xdx_90D_eus-gaap--AvailableForSaleDebtSecuritiesAmortizedCostBasis_iI_pn3n3_c20250331__us-gaap--StatementEquityComponentsAxis__custom--SeriesARedeemablePreferenceSecuritiesMember_zkYk5SOIERy7" title="Held-to-maturity investments, amortized cost basis"><ix:nonFraction name="us-gaap:AvailableForSaleDebtSecuritiesAmortizedCostBasis" contextRef="AsOf2025-03-31_custom_SeriesARedeemablePreferenceSecuritiesMember" id="Fact001261" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="-3" scale="3" unitRef="USD">1,008</ix:nonFraction></span>, respectively.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; text-align: justify; margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0">Prior to the Closing Date, WWAC modified the terms of payment owed to Shearman &amp; Sterling LLP, a multinational law firm providing legal consultancy services to WWAC. This resulted in a reduction in the total amount owed by WWAC to Shearman &amp; Sterling LLP from $4,800 of accounts payable to $4,000 promissory note, payable in four equal tranches. Subsequently, the promissory note was amended upon payment of $1,500, wherein the balance $2,500 was promised to be paid in two equal tranches. $2,500 owed to Shearman &amp; Sterling LLP has been disclosed as short-term debt, as ATI has an unconditional obligation to settle it within a period of less than twelve months from March&#160;31, 2026.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; text-align: justify; margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0"><span id="xdx_901_ecustom--InsuranceForItsDirectors_c20250401__20260331_zilpI7Yf2D5a" title="Insurance for its directors"><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="From2025-04-01to2026-03-31" id="Fact001303" name="aert:InsuranceForItsDirectors">After the Closing Date, ATI obtained an insurance policy for its directors and senior officers with $5,000 in coverage. The total premium payable in relation to this was $880 out of which $176 was paid upfront and balance $704 was payable in ten equal monthly instalments of $73. The arrangement represented a financing transaction where the premium payable was deferred. The interest rate under the arrangement was 9.2% per annum. The cumulative interest payable throughout the tenure under the arrangement amounts to $30 and the same was recognized as part of the interest expense in the consolidated statement of operations. During the year ended March&#160;31, 2026 and March&#160;31, 2025, the interest expense so recognized was Nil and $9. The balance premium payable as of March&#160;31, 2025 is Nil.</ix:nonNumeric></span></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; text-align: justify; margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0"><span id="xdx_900_ecustom--RenewedInsurancePolicyForItsDirectors_c20250401__20260331_zkUUwkjXd1Ji"><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="From2025-04-01to2026-03-31" id="Fact001304" name="aert:RenewedInsurancePolicyForItsDirectors">The
Company obtained an insurance policy for its directors and senior officers to cover $5,000, effective as of November&#160;6, 2024,
for a period of 12 months. The total premium payable under the insurance policy was $670, out of which $58 was paid upfront and the
$612 balance of which is payable in eleven equal monthly installments of $58. The arrangement represents a financing transaction
where the premium payable has been deferred. The interest payable under the arrangement amounts to $23 and the same would be
recognized as part of the interest expense through the condensed consolidated statement of operations.</ix:nonNumeric></span> During the year ended
March&#160;31, 2026 and March&#160;31, 2025, the interest expense so recognized was $<span id="xdx_90D_eus-gaap--InterestExpenseDebt_pn3n3_c20250401__20260331_zHwdRvBj84j5"><ix:nonFraction name="us-gaap:InterestExpenseDebt" contextRef="From2025-04-01to2026-03-31" id="Fact001305" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="-3" scale="3" unitRef="USD">0</ix:nonFraction></span>
and $<span id="xdx_906_eus-gaap--InterestExpenseDebt_pn3n3_c20240401__20250331_zuRn9W6bnF5e"><ix:nonFraction name="us-gaap:InterestExpenseDebt" contextRef="From2024-04-012025-03-31" id="Fact001306" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="-3" scale="3" unitRef="USD">16</ix:nonFraction></span> respectively. The balance

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; text-align: justify; margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0"><b><i>Contract balances</i></b></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; text-align: justify; margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0">Contract assets comprise amounts where the Company&#8217;s right to bill is contingent on something other than the passage of time. As of March&#160;31, 2026 and March&#160;31, 2025, the Company&#8217;s contract assets were $<span id="xdx_908_eus-gaap--ContractWithCustomerAssetNet_iI_pn3n3_c20260331_zOsgtmUzA7A5" title="Contract assets"><ix:nonFraction name="us-gaap:ContractWithCustomerAssetNet" contextRef="AsOf2026-03-31" id="Fact001415" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="-3" scale="3" unitRef="USD">166</ix:nonFraction></span> and $<span id="xdx_908_eus-gaap--ContractWithCustomerAssetNet_iI_pn3n3_c20250331_zbmyZnRVlJA7" title="Contract assets"><ix:nonFraction name="us-gaap:ContractWithCustomerAssetNet" contextRef="AsOf2025-03-31" id="Fact001417" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="-3" scale="3" unitRef="USD">163</ix:nonFraction></span>, respectively, and were recorded within &#8220;Prepaid expenses and other current assets&#8221;, net of allowance for credit losses, on the consolidated balance sheets.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; text-align: justify; margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0">Contract liabilities, or deferred revenue, comprise amounts collected from the Company&#8217;s customers for revenues not yet earned and amounts which are anticipated to be recorded as revenues when services are performed. The amount of revenue recognized in the year ended March&#160;31, 2026 and 2025 that was included in deferred revenue at the beginning of each period was $<span id="xdx_901_eus-gaap--DeferredIncomeRevenueRecognized_pn3n3_c20250401__20260331_zriC5Wzjttwh" title="Deferred revenue recognized"><ix:nonFraction name="us-gaap:DeferredIncomeRevenueRecognized" contextRef="From2025-04-01to2026-03-31" id="Fact001419" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="-3" scale="3" unitRef="USD">249</ix:nonFraction></span> and $<span id="xdx_90C_eus-gaap--DeferredIncomeRevenueRecognized_pn3n3_c20240401__20250331_zyLdfzDjhag1" title="Deferred revenue recognized"><ix:nonFraction name="us-gaap:DeferredIncomeRevenueRecognized" contextRef="From2024-04-012025-03-31" id="Fact001421" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="-3" scale="3" unitRef="USD">257</ix:nonFraction></span>, respectively.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; text-align: justify; margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0">As of March&#160;31, 2026 and March&#160;31, 2025 the Company&#8217;s deferred revenue was $<span id="xdx_90B_eus-gaap--DeferredRevenue_iI_pn3n3_c20260331_zKnNhHJQgfx5" title="Deferred revenue"><ix:nonFraction name="us-gaap:DeferredRevenue" contextRef="AsOf2026-03-31" id="Fact001423" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="-3" scale="3" unitRef="USD">466</ix:nonFraction></span> and $<span id="xdx_908_eus-gaap--DeferredRevenue_iI_pn3n3_c20250331_zGWeo5DhhRxc" title="Deferred revenue"><ix:nonFraction name="us-gaap:DeferredRevenue" contextRef="AsOf2025-03-31" id="Fact001425" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="-3" scale="3" unitRef="USD">274</ix:nonFraction></span>, respectively, and was recorded within &#8220;Other current liabilities&#8221; on the consolidated balance sheets. There was <span id="xdx_90A_eus-gaap--DeferredRevenueNoncurrent_iI_pn3n3_do_c20260331_zxVvtCqEyOxa" title="Deferred revenue, non current"><span id="xdx_901_eus-gaap--DeferredRevenueNoncurrent_iI_pn3n3_do_c20250331_ztcyy6TKE6Rl" title="Deferred revenue, non current"><ix:nonFraction name="us-gaap:DeferredRevenueNoncurrent" contextRef="AsOf2026-03-31" id="Fact001427" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen" decimals="-3" scale="3" unitRef="USD"><ix:nonFraction name="us-gaap:DeferredRevenueNoncurrent" contextRef="AsOf2025-03-31" id="Fact001429" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen" decimals="-3" scale="3" unitRef="USD">no</ix:nonFraction></ix:nonFraction></span></span> deferred revenue classified as non-current as of March&#160;31, 2026 and March&#160;31, 2025.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; text-align: justify; margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0"><b><i>Contract Acquisition Costs</i></b></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; text-align: justify; margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0">Direct and incremental costs incurred for acquiring contracts, such as sales commissions are contract acquisition costs and thereby classified under &#8220;Other current assets&#8221; and &#8220;Other assets&#8221; in the consolidated balance sheets. Such costs are amortized over the expected duration of the relationship with customers and recorded under Selling and marketing expenses in the consolidated statements of income.</p>

</ix:nonNumeric><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="From2025-04-01to2026-03-31" escape="true" id="Fact001432" name="us-gaap:CompensationAndEmployeeBenefitPlansTextBlock"><p id="xdx_804_eus-gaap--CompensationAndEmployeeBenefitPlansTextBlock_zZcIZoE3cQDd" style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; text-align: justify; margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0"><b>Note 11 - <span id="xdx_820_zIcKNdZlNyUb">Employee Compensation and Benefits</span></b></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; text-align: justify; margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0">The Company has employee benefit plans in the form of certain statutory and other programs covering its employees.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; text-align: justify; margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0"><b><i>Defined Benefit Plan - Gratuity</i></b></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; text-align: justify; margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0">The Company has subsidiaries in India and Mexico with employees covered by defined benefit plans. We have defined benefit plans comprised of gratuity under Payments of Gratuity Act, 1972 covering eligible employees in India &amp; Federal Labor Law in Mexico. The present value of the defined benefit obligations and other long-term employee benefits is determined based on actuarial valuation using the projected unit credit method. The rate used to discount defined benefit obligation is determined by reference to market yields at the balance sheet date of government bonds for respective regions for the estimated term of obligations.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; text-align: justify; margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0">Actuarial gains or losses arising on account of experience adjustment and the effect of changes in actuarial assumptions are initially recognized in the consolidated statements of comprehensive income, and the unrecognized actuarial loss is amortized to the consolidated statements of operations over the average remaining service period of the active employees expected to receive benefits under the plan.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; text-align: justify; margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; text-align: justify; margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0">On November&#160;21, 2025, the Government of India notified provisions of the Labour Codes - the Code on Wages, 2019, the Industrial Relations Code, 2020, the Code on Social Security, 2020, and the Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions Code, 2020 - consolidating 29 existing labour laws. The Ministry of Labour &amp; Employment published draft Central Rules and FAQs to enable assessment of the financial impact due to changes in regulations. The Group continues to monitor the finalisation of Central / State Rules and clarifications from the Government on other aspects of the Labour Code and would provide appropriate accounting effect on the basis of such developments as needed. The adjustments for the Labour Codes represent an increase in gratuity liability arising out of past service cost by $703 primarily due to change in wage definition which is recognized in the other comprehensive income / (loss), net of tax. Out of the above, $62 is reclassified to Consolidated Statement of Operations for the year ended March&#160;31, 2026.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; text-align: justify; margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0">The following table provides the status of the defined benefit plans and the amounts recognized in the Company&#8217;s consolidated financial statements based on actuarial valuations carried out for the periods ending March&#160;31, 2026 and March&#160;31, 2025, respectively:</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; text-align: justify; margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0"><i>Assumptions</i></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; text-align: justify; margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0">The Company uses the Projected Unit Credit Method to measure liabilities and interest costs for defined benefit obligations. Under this method, accrued benefit amount is projected to calculate future expected cashflows, which is in turn discounted back at applicable discount rate assumption to arrive at present value of benefit obligation.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; text-align: justify; margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0">The rate used to discount benefit obligations (both funded and unfunded) is determined by reference to market yields on government bonds at the balance sheet date. The currency and term of the government bonds should be consistent with the currency and estimated term of the benefit obligations.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; text-align: justify; margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0">The weighted average assumptions used to determine the benefit obligations of the defined benefit plans as of March&#160;31, 2026 and 2025 are presented below:</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; text-align: justify; margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0"><i>Net operating loss</i></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; text-align: justify; margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0">The Company has carry forward losses of $<span id="xdx_902_eus-gaap--OperatingLossCarryforwards_iI_pn3n3_c20290331_zvmqqLY8bh7a" title="Net operating loss"><ix:nonFraction name="us-gaap:OperatingLossCarryforwards" contextRef="AsOf2029-03-31" id="Fact001983" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="-3" scale="3" unitRef="USD">35</ix:nonFraction></span>, $<span id="xdx_907_eus-gaap--OperatingLossCarryforwards_iI_pn3n3_c20300331_z4Oqh5vrlfGd" title="Net operating loss"><ix:nonFraction name="us-gaap:OperatingLossCarryforwards" contextRef="AsOf2030-03-31" id="Fact001985" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="-3" scale="3" unitRef="USD">70</ix:nonFraction></span> &amp; $<span id="xdx_907_eus-gaap--OperatingLossCarryforwards_iI_pn3n3_c20330331_zgKWYVqV8pQl" title="Net operating loss"><ix:nonFraction name="us-gaap:OperatingLossCarryforwards" contextRef="AsOf2033-03-31" id="Fact001987" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="-3" scale="3" unitRef="USD">2,975</ix:nonFraction></span> in the Indian jurisdiction, which will get expired in financial years 2028-29; 2029-30 and 2032-33 respectively.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; text-align: justify; margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0">With certain immaterial exceptions, the Company is no longer subject to U.S. federal, state and local or other U.S. income tax examinations by taxing authorities for years prior to 2022. The Company&#8217;s subsidiaries in India are open to examination by relevant taxing authorities for tax years beginning on or after April&#160;1, 2016. The Company regularly reviews the likelihood of additional tax assessments and adjusts its unrecognized tax benefits as additional information or events require.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; text-align: justify; margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0">Valuation Allowances</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; text-align: justify; margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0">As of March&#160;31, 2026, the Company maintained valuation allowances of $2,749 for deferred tax assets that are not more likely than not to be realized, which primarily included deferred tax assets towards Net Operating Losses (NOL) in Singapore and UAE jurisdictions. The valuation allowances on our deferred tax assets decreased by $<span id="xdx_905_eus-gaap--DeferredTaxAssetsValuationAllowance_iI_pn3n3_c20260331_ztHvAwTxXi47" title="Valuation allowances"><ix:nonFraction name="us-gaap:DeferredTaxAssetsValuationAllowance" contextRef="AsOf2026-03-31" id="Fact001989" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="-3" scale="3" unitRef="USD">122</ix:nonFraction></span> in year ended March&#160;31, 2026 as compared to increase by $<span id="xdx_904_eus-gaap--DeferredTaxAssetsValuationAllowance_iI_pn3n3_c20250331_zpzjeT3XpVfd" title="Valuation allowances"><ix:nonFraction name="us-gaap:DeferredTaxAssetsValuationAllowance" contextRef="AsOf2025-03-31" id="Fact001991" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="-3" scale="3" unitRef="USD">2,871</ix:nonFraction></span> during the year ended March&#160;31, 2025, respectively. During the year ended March&#160;2026, based on the relevant weight of positive and negative evidence, including the amount of net operating losses in recent years, and consideration of our future taxable earnings, we concluded most of our Singapore and UAE deferred tax assets are not more like than to be realized. Our deferred tax assets without valuation allowances are more like than not to be realized given the expectation of future earnings in the respective jurisdictions.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; text-align: justify; margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0"><i>Unrecognized tax benefits</i></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; text-align: justify; margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0">The Company recognizes financial statement benefit of a tax position only after determining that the relevant tax authority would more-likely-than-not sustain the position following an audit. As of March&#160;31, 2026 and March&#160;31, 2025, the Company does <span id="xdx_90C_eus-gaap--UnrecognizedTaxBenefits_iI_pn3n3_do_c20250331_zVyHYDDy5bc1" title="Unrecognized tax benefits"><span id="xdx_90C_eus-gaap--UnrecognizedTaxBenefits_iI_pn3n3_do_c20260331_z9F2od7TGzqi" title="Unrecognized tax benefits"><ix:nonFraction name="us-gaap:UnrecognizedTaxBenefits" contextRef="AsOf2025-03-31" id="Fact001993" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen" decimals="-3" scale="3" unitRef="USD"><ix:nonFraction name="us-gaap:UnrecognizedTaxBenefits" contextRef="AsOf2026-03-31" id="Fact001995" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen" decimals="-3" scale="3" unitRef="USD">no</ix:nonFraction></ix:nonFraction></span></span>t have any unrecognized tax benefits with a significant impact on its consolidated financial statements.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; text-align: justify; margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0">The Company&#8217;s major tax jurisdictions are Singapore, India, the United States, and Mexico. Generally accepted accounting principles requires the Company&#8217;s management to evaluate tax positions taken by the Company and recognize a tax liability for any uncertain positions that more likely than not would not be sustained upon examination by the Internal Revenue System (the &#8220;IRS&#8221;) or a foreign jurisdiction taxing authority. The Company is subject to routine audits by tax authorities.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; text-align: justify; margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0">Deferred tax has not been recognized on the excess of the amount for financial reporting over the tax basis of investments in foreign subsidiaries that is indefinitely reinvested. This amount becomes taxable upon a repatriation of assets from the subsidiary or a sale or liquidation of the subsidiary. The amount of such temporary differences totaled approximately $10,435, with an income tax impact of approximately $1,454 as of March&#160;31, 2026.</p>

</ix:nonNumeric><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="From2025-04-01to2026-03-31" escape="true" id="Fact002170" name="us-gaap:CompensationRelatedCostsGeneralTextBlock"><p id="xdx_80F_eus-gaap--CompensationRelatedCostsGeneralTextBlock_zGMaoNBu4j0j" style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; text-align: justify; margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0"><b>Note 14 - <span id="xdx_827_zR21h2yxhXD7">Stock-Based Compensation</span></b></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; text-align: justify; margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0"><b>Aeries Technology, Inc. 2023 Equity Incentive Plan</b></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; text-align: justify; margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0">The board of directors of WWAC approved the Aeries Technology, Inc. 2023 Equity Incentive Plan (the &#8220;Plan&#8221;) on March&#160;11, 2023, subject to approval by WWAC&#8217;s shareholders. The Plan was approved by WWAC&#8217;s shareholders on November&#160;2, 2023 and the Plan became effective upon the consummation of the Business Combination. The number of Class A ordinary shares authorized for issuance under the Plan is <span id="xdx_909_eus-gaap--StockIssuedDuringPeriodSharesNewIssues_pid_c20231028__20231102_zPzv4a8ZeUMc" title="Number of shares issued"><ix:nonFraction name="us-gaap:StockIssuedDuringPeriodSharesNewIssues" contextRef="From2023-10-282023-11-02" id="Fact002172" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="INF" unitRef="Shares">9,031,027</ix:nonFraction></span>, subject to certain adjustments set forth in the Plan.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; text-align: justify; margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0">On March&#160;27, 2025, at the Company&#8217;s annual meeting of the shareholders, the Company&#8217;s shareholders approved Amendment No. 1 (the &#8220;Plan Amendment&#8221;) to the Plan. The Plan Amendment provided for (i) increasing the total number of Class A ordinary shares authorized under the Plan to <span id="xdx_909_eus-gaap--StockIssuedDuringPeriodSharesNewIssues_pid_c20250301__20250327_zwFIdbzig7H7" title="Number of shares issued"><ix:nonFraction name="us-gaap:StockIssuedDuringPeriodSharesNewIssues" contextRef="From2025-03-012025-03-27" id="Fact002174" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="INF" unitRef="Shares">11,928,287</ix:nonFraction></span> shares (the &#8220;New Share Reserve&#8221;), (ii) amending the &#8220;evergreen&#8221; provision in the Plan to automatically increase the New Share Reserve by 5% on an annual basis or by such lesser amount that the compensation committee of the board of directors may determine (&#8220;Evergreen Increase&#8221;), and (iii) removing the annual limits on issuing awards to a single individual under Sections&#160;5(d) and 5(e) of the Plan.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; text-align: justify; margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0">On December&#160;26, 2025, the Company&#8217;s board of directors approved <span id="xdx_909_ecustom--AdditionalSharesToBeAvailableForIssuance_c20251201__20251226_pd" title="Additional shares to be available for issuance"><ix:nonFraction name="aert:AdditionalSharesToBeAvailableForIssuance" contextRef="From2025-12-012025-12-26" id="Fact002176" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="INF" unitRef="Shares">2,227,899</ix:nonFraction></span> additional shares to be available for issuance under the Plan pursuant to the Evergreen Increase provision.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; text-align: justify; margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0"><b>Restricted Share Unit Award</b></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; text-align: justify; margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0">Compensation cost for stock awards, which include restricted stock units (&#8220;RSUs&#8221;), is measured at the fair value on the grant date and recognized as expense, net of estimated forfeitures. The fair value of stock awards is based on the quoted price of our Class A ordinary shares on the grant date. We measure the fair value of RSUs using fair value of our quoted stock due to grant date and vesting date being same. Compensation cost for RSUs is recognized on a straight line over vesting period.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; text-align: justify; margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0">The Company&#8217;s board of directors approved the below grant of restricted stock unit awards (&#8220;RSUs&#8221;) under the Plan on September&#160;9, 2025.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; text-align: justify; margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0"><b>Non-Employee Director Equity Compensation</b></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; text-align: justify; margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0">Pursuant to the Plan, the Company granted the non-employee directors, Ms. Nina B. Shapiro, Mr. Biswajit Dasgupta and Mr. Alok Kochhar, <span id="xdx_90A_eus-gaap--ShareBasedCompensationArrangementByShareBasedPaymentAwardOptionsGrantsInPeriod_pid_c20250901__20250909__srt--CounterpartyNameAxis__custom--MsNinaBShapiroMember_zMqpJuZJRSXd" title="Shares granted"><span id="xdx_90E_eus-gaap--ShareBasedCompensationArrangementByShareBasedPaymentAwardOptionsGrantsInPeriod_pid_c20250901__20250909__srt--CounterpartyNameAxis__custom--MrBiswajitDasguptaMember_zEOGE4VS0hdc" title="Shares granted"><span id="xdx_90C_eus-gaap--ShareBasedCompensationArrangementByShareBasedPaymentAwardOptionsGrantsInPeriod_pid_c20250901__20250909__srt--CounterpartyNameAxis__custom--MrAlokKochharMember_zTGEiaoHXHIc" title="Shares granted"><ix:nonFraction name="us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensationArrangementByShareBasedPaymentAwardOptionsGrantsInPeriod" contextRef="From2025-09-012025-09-09_custom_MsNinaBShapiroMember" id="Fact002178" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="INF" unitRef="Shares"><ix:nonFraction name="us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensationArrangementByShareBasedPaymentAwardOptionsGrantsInPeriod" contextRef="From2025-09-012025-09-09_custom_MrBiswajitDasguptaMember" id="Fact002180" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="INF" unitRef="Shares"><ix:nonFraction name="us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensationArrangementByShareBasedPaymentAwardOptionsGrantsInPeriod" contextRef="From2025-09-012025-09-09_custom_MrAlokKochharMember" id="Fact002182" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="INF" unitRef="Shares">125,000</ix:nonFraction></ix:nonFraction></ix:nonFraction></span></span></span> RSUs each on September&#160;9, 2025, which were fully vested on the grant date.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; text-align: justify; margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0"><b>Consultant Equity Compensation</b></p>

</ix:nonNumeric><p id="xdx_8A0_zL99xiMfI5P8" style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; text-align: justify; margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0"><b>Aeries Employees Stock Option Plan, 2020</b></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; text-align: justify; margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0">On August&#160;1, 2020, ATGBA&#8217;s board of directors approved and executed the Aeries Employees Stock Option Plan (&#8220;ESOP&#8221;), which was subsequently amended on July&#160;22, 2022. Under ESOP, the company is authorized to grant up to <span id="xdx_906_eus-gaap--StockIssuedDuringPeriodSharesShareBasedCompensation_pid_c20200730__20200801_z9iycpsaY855" title="Shares issued under ESOP"><ix:nonFraction name="us-gaap:StockIssuedDuringPeriodSharesShareBasedCompensation" contextRef="From2020-07-302020-08-01" id="Fact002229" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="INF" unitRef="Shares">59,900</ix:nonFraction></span> options to eligible employees in one or more tranches. The company granted <span id="xdx_90B_eus-gaap--StockIssuedDuringPeriodSharesShareBasedCompensation_pid_c20220401__20230331_zj3dW0qAKAY6" title="Shares issued under ESOP"><ix:nonFraction name="us-gaap:StockIssuedDuringPeriodSharesShareBasedCompensation" contextRef="From2022-04-012023-03-31" id="Fact002231" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="INF" unitRef="Shares">59,900</ix:nonFraction></span> options to eligible employees during the year ended March&#160;31, 2023.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; text-align: justify; margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0">The options issued under the ESOP generally are subject to service conditions. The service condition is typically one year. The stock-based compensation expense is recognized in the consolidated statements of comprehensive income using the straight-line attribution method over the requisite service period.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; text-align: justify; margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0">The following table summarizes the ESOP stock option activity for the year ended March&#160;31, 2026:</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; text-align: justify; margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0"><b>Aeries Management Stock Option Plan, 2019</b></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; text-align: justify; margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0">On September&#160;23, 2019, ATGBA&#8217;s board of directors approved and executed the Aeries Management Stock Option Plan 2019 (&#8220;MSOP&#8221;), which was subsequently amended on September&#160;30, 2022. Under MSOP, ATGBA has authorized to grant up to <span id="xdx_903_eus-gaap--StockIssuedDuringPeriodSharesShareBasedCompensation_pid_c20190901__20190923_zWYecGBah7gg" title="Shares issued under ESOP"><ix:nonFraction name="us-gaap:StockIssuedDuringPeriodSharesShareBasedCompensation" contextRef="From2019-09-012019-09-23" id="Fact002271" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="INF" unitRef="Shares">295,565</ix:nonFraction></span> options to eligible employees in one or more tranches.</p>





<ix:exclude><p id="xdx_23E_zqGuNnExPtJ9" style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0">&#160;</p></ix:exclude>



<ix:exclude><!-- Field: Page; Sequence: 142; Value: 1 -->
    <div style="border-bottom: Black 2pt solid; margin-top: 6pt; margin-bottom: 6pt"><p style="font: normal 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; text-align: center; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt">F-<!-- Field: Sequence; Type: Arabic; Name: PageNo -->39<!-- Field: /Sequence --></p></div>
    <div style="break-before: page; margin-top: 6pt; margin-bottom: 6pt"><p style="text-align: center; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt">&#160;</p></div>
    <!-- Field: /Page --></ix:exclude>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; text-align: justify; margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0">The options issued under the MSOP generally are subject to both service and performance conditions. The service condition is typically one year, and the performance conditions are based on the consolidated revenue and adjusted profit before tax of ATGBA. The stock-based compensation expense is recognized in the consolidated statements of comprehensive income using the straight-line attribution method over the requisite service period if it is probable that the performance target will be achieved.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; text-align: justify; margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0">During the year ended March&#160;31, 2026, 236,455 options under MSOP, that were fully vested expired unexercised upon reaching the end of their term. As these options were vested, no reversal of previously recognized share-based compensation expense was recorded upon expiration in the condensed consolidated statement of operations for the year ended March&#160;31, 2026. The excess of previously recognized compensation expense related to these options has been reclassified from stock option reserve classified under additional paid-in capital to additional paid-in capital &#8211; other reserve.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; text-align: justify; margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0">Further, tor the year ended March&#160;31, 2026, <span id="xdx_907_ecustom--MsopExercisedDescription_c20250401__20260331_zvgQaZD51Efe" title="MSOP exercised description"><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="From2025-04-01to2026-03-31" id="Fact002274" name="aert:MsopExercisedDescription">the balance 59,110 options under MSOP were exercised by Mr. Bhisham (Ajay) Khare with exercise price of INR 10 (or approximately $0.11 at the exchange rate in effect on March&#160;31, 2026). As on March&#160;31, 2026, a remittance in transit of $6.24 has been recognized in respect of the exercise price of such options.</ix:nonNumeric></span></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; text-align: justify; margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0">The following table summarizes the MSOP stock option activity for the year ended March&#160;31, 2026:</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; text-align: justify; margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0">The Company uses the BSM option-pricing model to determine the grant-date fair value of stock options. The determination of the fair value of stock options on the grant date is affected by the estimated underlying share price, as well as assumptions regarding a number of complex and subjective variables. These variables include expected stock price volatility over the term of the awards, actual and projected employee stock option exercise behaviors, risk-free interest rates, and expected dividends. The grant date fair value of the Company&#8217;s stock options granted to employees were estimated using the Black-Scholes option-pricing model with the following weighted average assumptions:</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; text-align: justify; margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0"><b>Indemnification obligations</b></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; text-align: justify; margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0">In the normal course of business, the Company is a party to a variety of agreements under which it may be obligated to indemnify the other party for certain matters. These obligations typically arise in contracts where the Company customarily agrees to hold the other party harmless against losses arising from a breach of representations or covenants for certain matters, infringement of third-party intellectual property rights, data privacy violations, and certain tortious conduct in the course of providing services. The duration of these indemnifications varies, and in certain cases, is indefinite.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; text-align: justify; margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0">The Company is unable to reasonably estimate the maximum potential amount of future payments under these or similar agreements due to the unique facts and circumstances of each agreement and the fact that certain indemnifications provide for no limitation to the maximum potential future payments under the indemnification. Management is not aware of any such matters that would have a material effect on the consolidated financial statements of the Company.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; text-align: justify; margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0"><b>Exchange Agreements</b></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; text-align: justify; margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0">Upon consummation of the Business Combination, the holders of AARK ordinary shares and ATGBA ordinary shares each entered into the Exchange Agreements. Pursuant to the Exchange Agreements, from and after the date of the Exchange Agreements and prior to April&#160;1, 2024 and subject to certain exercise conditions, each holder of AARK ordinary shares and ATGBA ordinary shares may exchange up to 20% of the number of AARK ordinary shares and ATGBA ordinary shares, as applicable, held by such holder for Class A ordinary shares of the Company or cash, in each case as provided in the Exchange Agreements. From and after April&#160;1, 2024 and subject to certain exercise conditions, the Company shall have the right to acquire all of the AARK or ATGBA ordinary Share for Class A ordinary shares or cash. In addition, after April&#160;1, 2024 and subject to certain exercise condition, each shareholder of ATGBA and AARK ordinary shares shall have the right to require the Company to provide Class A ordinary shares or cash in exchange for up to all of the AARK or ATGBA ordinary share. Each share of AARK may be exchanged for 2,246 Class A ordinary shares the Company and each ATGBA ordinary share may be exchanged for 14.40 Class A ordinary shares of the Company, in each case subject to certain adjustments. The cash exchange payment may only be elected in the event approval from the Reserve Bank of India is not obtained for exchange of shares and provided that the Company has reasonable cash flow to be able to pay the cash exchange payment and such payment would not be prohibited by any then outstanding debt agreements or arrangements of the Company.</p>

</ix:nonNumeric><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="From2025-04-01to2026-03-31" escape="true" id="Fact002465" name="aert:DisclosureOfWarrantLiabilityTextBlock"><p id="xdx_80C_ecustom--DisclosureOfWarrantLiabilityTextBlock_zI9xt3FqL7g" style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; text-align: justify; margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0"><b>Note 17 - <span id="xdx_82F_z4Lzb3eppiy">Warrant Liabilities</span></b></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; text-align: justify; margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0">On October&#160;22, 2021, pursuant to <span id="xdx_904_ecustom--InitialPublicOfferingDescription_c20250401__20260331_zgS2foIuIcSf" title="Initial public offering description"><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="From2025-04-01to2026-03-31" id="Fact002467" name="aert:InitialPublicOfferingDescription">the consummation of the Initial Public Offering, the Company issued 11,499,991 Public Warrants. Simultaneously with the closing of the Initial Public Offering, WWAC issued 8,900,000 warrants in a private placement (the &#8220;Private Placement Warrants&#8221;), at a purchase price of $1.00 per Private Placement Warrant, which included 900,000 units as a result of the underwriter&#8217;s full exercise of its option to purchase up to 900,000 additional warrants, at a purchase price of $1.00 per Private Placement Warrant. On November&#160;6, 2023, WWAC issued 627,810 other Private Placement Warrants to the Sponsor pursuant to the conversion of a promissory note payable to the Sponsor. Upon consummation of the Business Combination, the Company assumed 11,499,991 Public Warrants and 9,527,810 Private Placement Warrants (collectively the &#8220;Warrants&#8221;).</ix:nonNumeric></span></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; text-align: justify; margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0">The Company accounted for the Warrants in accordance with the guidance contained in ASC 815-40 given that certain provisions within the warrant agreement either preclude the warrants from being considered indexed to the ATI&#8217;s own stock or the fixed-for-fixed option criteria are not met. On this basis the Public and Private Placement Warrants are classified as a liability and are measured at fair value. This liability is subject to re-measurement at each balance sheet date. With each such re-measurement, the warrant liability will be adjusted to fair value, with the change in fair value recognized in the Company&#8217;s consolidated statement of operations.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; text-align: justify; margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0">Each whole Warrant entitles the holder thereof to purchase one Class A ordinary share of the Company, par value $0.0001 per share, for $<span id="xdx_907_eus-gaap--ClassOfWarrantOrRightExercisePriceOfWarrantsOrRights1_iI_pid_c20260331__us-gaap--ClassOfWarrantOrRightAxis__custom--PublicWarrantsMember_zWKksfxBgE1" title="Exercise price of warrants"><ix:nonFraction name="us-gaap:ClassOfWarrantOrRightExercisePriceOfWarrantsOrRights1" contextRef="AsOf2026-03-31_custom_PublicWarrantsMember" id="Fact002469" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="INF" unitRef="USDPShares">11.50</ix:nonFraction></span> per share, subject to adjustment as described herein. Only whole Warrants are exercisable. A holder of the Warrants will not be able to exercise any fraction of a Warrant. The Warrants will expire at 5:00 p.m. New York City time on November&#160;6, 2028, or earlier upon redemption or liquidation. On the exercise of any Warrant, the Warrant exercise price will be paid directly to us.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; text-align: justify; margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0">A share repurchase program has been approved by the board on February&#160;25, 2026 (the &#8220;Repurchase Program&#8221;) pursuant to which the Company may repurchase up to $<span id="xdx_90E_ecustom--StocksRepurchasedDuringPeriodValue_pn3n3_c20260201__20260225_zappEpCfnvo6" title="Shares repurchsed, amount"><ix:nonFraction name="aert:StocksRepurchasedDuringPeriodValue" contextRef="From2026-02-012026-02-25" id="Fact002499" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="-3" scale="3" unitRef="USD">5,000</ix:nonFraction></span> of the Company&#8217;s Class A ordinary shares to be effected over a period of twelve (12) months.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; text-align: justify; margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0">In connection therewith, the
board approved the adoption of a Rule&#160;10b5-1 issuer share repurchase trading plan on March&#160;23, 2026 (the &#8220;Trading Plan&#8221;),
pursuant to which the Company may repurchase its ordinary shares from time to time in accordance with applicable laws and regulations,
including Rule&#160;10b5-1 under the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, as amended. Maximum amount for cumulative purchases under the Trading
Plan will not exceed $3,000 (exclusive of commission). The Company&#8217;s share repurchase program does not obligate the Company to
acquire a minimum amount of shares. Under the program, shares may be repurchased in privately negotiated or open market transactions,
including under plans complying with Rule&#160;10b5-1 under the Exchange Act.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; text-align: justify; margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0">During the period ending March&#160;31, 2026, the Company repurchased <span id="xdx_900_eus-gaap--StockRepurchasedDuringPeriodShares_pid_c20250401__20260331_zHGQFK0iZPN2" title="Shares repurchsed, shares"><ix:nonFraction name="us-gaap:StockRepurchasedDuringPeriodShares" contextRef="From2025-04-01to2026-03-31" id="Fact002501" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="INF" unitRef="Shares">1,712,562</ix:nonFraction></span> shares of its common stock for $<span id="xdx_909_ecustom--StocksRepurchasedDuringPeriodValue_pn3n3_c20250401__20260331_z25dERnqqeTd" title="Shares repurchsed, amount"><ix:nonFraction name="aert:StocksRepurchasedDuringPeriodValue" contextRef="From2025-04-01to2026-03-31" id="Fact002503" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="-3" scale="3" unitRef="USD">580</ix:nonFraction></span> inclusive of commission to be held as treasury stock at cost according to ASC 505.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; text-align: justify; margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0"><b>Class V ordinary shares</b></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; text-align: justify; margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0">The Company is authorized to issue 1 Class V ordinary share with a par value of $0.0001 per share. As of March&#160;31, 2026, there was 1 Class V ordinary share issued and outstanding. The Class V share does not carry any direct economic rights in dividends and other distributions or in an event of liquidation. It does carry voting rights equal to 1.3% which will ratchet up to 51% voting rights upon occurrence of &#8220;extraordinary events&#8221; at the ATI level.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; text-align: justify; margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0"><b>Common stock</b></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; text-align: justify; margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0">Pre-combination AARK had only one class of ordinary shares having no par value. Holders of ordinary shares were entitled to one vote per share held. As of June&#160;14, 2023 (immediately prior to the effective date of a stock split), there were 10 ordinary shares outstanding, and the number of ordinary shares outstanding after a stock split was <span id="xdx_900_eus-gaap--StockIssuedDuringPeriodSharesStockSplits_pid_c20230601__20230614_zOLr4AZ6Iz2j" title="Number of shares of common stock outstanding after stock split"><ix:nonFraction name="us-gaap:StockIssuedDuringPeriodSharesStockSplits" contextRef="From2023-06-012023-06-14" id="Fact002524" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="INF" unitRef="Shares">10,000</ix:nonFraction></span>. As a result of stock split, AARK&#8217;s shares were retroactively restated as if the transaction occurred at the beginning of the earliest periods presented. Consequently, as of April&#160;1 2023 and 2022, the AARK&#8217;s ordinary shares consisted of <span id="xdx_90B_eus-gaap--CommonStockSharesIssued_iI_pid_c20230402_zxEmiEifbyl1" title="Common stock, shares issued"><span id="xdx_904_eus-gaap--CommonStockSharesIssued_iI_pid_c20220402_z3fXrCoVU5C1" title="Common stock, shares issued"><ix:nonFraction name="us-gaap:CommonStockSharesIssued" contextRef="AsOf2023-04-02" id="Fact002526" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="INF" unitRef="Shares"><ix:nonFraction name="us-gaap:CommonStockSharesIssued" contextRef="AsOf2022-04-02" id="Fact002528" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="INF" unitRef="Shares">10,000</ix:nonFraction></ix:nonFraction></span></span> shares, all of which were issued and fully paid. Upon the liquidation, dissolution or winding up of AARK, ordinary shareholders were entitled to receive a ratable share of the available net assets of AARK after payment of all debts and other liabilities. The ordinary shares had no preemptive, subscription, redemption or conversion rights.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; text-align: justify; margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0"><b>Equity financing</b></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; text-align: justify; margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0">On April&#160;8, 2024, the Company entered into a private placement transaction (the &#8220;Private Placement&#8221;), pursuant to a Share Subscription Agreement (the &#8220;Subscription Agreement&#8221;) with an institutional accredited investor (the &#8220;Investor&#8221;) for aggregate gross proceeds of $<span id="xdx_90C_eus-gaap--ProceedsFromCustomers_pn3n3_c20240401__20240408__us-gaap--TypeOfArrangementAxis__custom--SubscriptionAgreementMember__us-gaap--RelatedPartyTransactionsByRelatedPartyAxis__us-gaap--InvestorMember_zcB0U8eF6hYk" title="Gross proceeds"><ix:nonFraction name="us-gaap:ProceedsFromCustomers" contextRef="From2024-04-012024-04-08_custom_SubscriptionAgreementMember_us-gaap_InvestorMember" id="Fact002531" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="-3" scale="3" unitRef="USD">5,000</ix:nonFraction></span>. The Private Placement closed on April&#160;23, 2024. As part of the Private Placement, the Company agreed to sell an aggregate of <span id="xdx_90D_ecustom--OrdinaryShares_iI_pid_c20240408__us-gaap--TypeOfArrangementAxis__custom--SubscriptionAgreementMember_zlinsXU05yah" title="Ordinary shares"><ix:nonFraction name="aert:OrdinaryShares" contextRef="AsOf2024-04-08_custom_SubscriptionAgreementMember" id="Fact002533" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="INF" unitRef="Shares">2,261,778</ix:nonFraction></span> Class A ordinary shares, $0.0001 par value per share, at a purchase price of $<span id="xdx_907_ecustom--PurchasePrice_pid_c20240401__20240408__us-gaap--TypeOfArrangementAxis__custom--SubscriptionAgreementMember__us-gaap--RelatedPartyTransactionsByRelatedPartyAxis__us-gaap--InvestorMember_zPyth5AAEpEd" title="Purchase price"><ix:nonFraction name="aert:PurchasePrice" contextRef="From2024-04-012024-04-08_custom_SubscriptionAgreementMember_us-gaap_InvestorMember" id="Fact002535" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="INF" unitRef="USDPShares">2.21</ix:nonFraction></span> per share subject to the Beneficial Ownership Limitation. The &#8220;Beneficial Ownership Limitation&#8221; shall be 4.99% (or, at the election of the Investor at the closing of the Private Placement, 9.99%) of the number of Class A ordinary shares outstanding immediately after giving effect to the issuance of the Class A ordinary shares to the Investor.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; text-align: justify; margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0"><span id="xdx_908_ecustom--CustomaryRepresentationsWarrantiesAndCovenantsOfParties_c20240401__20240408__us-gaap--TypeOfArrangementAxis__custom--SubscriptionAgreementMember_zGipl06ZEu6k" title="Customary representations, warranties and covenants of the parties"><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="From2024-04-012024-04-08_custom_SubscriptionAgreementMember" id="Fact002537" name="aert:CustomaryRepresentationsWarrantiesAndCovenantsOfParties">The Subscription Agreement contains customary representations, warranties and covenants of the parties, and the closing was subject to customary closing conditions. The Company used the net proceeds of approximately $4,675 from the Private Placement, following a deduction of a 6.5% commission paid to a placement agent, for general corporate and working capital purposes.</ix:nonNumeric></span></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; text-align: justify; margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0">As of the closing of the Private Placement, the Company issued an aggregate of <span id="xdx_904_eus-gaap--StockIssuedDuringPeriodSharesOther_pid_c20240401__20240408__us-gaap--TypeOfArrangementAxis__custom--SubscriptionAgreementMember__us-gaap--StatementClassOfStockAxis__custom--ClassAOrdinarySharesMember_z8t1jdWubacb" title="Number of shares issued"><ix:nonFraction name="us-gaap:StockIssuedDuringPeriodSharesOther" contextRef="From2024-04-012024-04-08_custom_SubscriptionAgreementMember_custom_ClassAOrdinarySharesMember" id="Fact002539" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="INF" unitRef="Shares">1,940,958</ix:nonFraction></span> Class A ordinary shares at a purchase price of $<span id="xdx_90F_ecustom--PurchasePrice_pid_c20240401__20240408__us-gaap--TypeOfArrangementAxis__custom--SubscriptionAgreementMember__us-gaap--StatementClassOfStockAxis__custom--ClassAOrdinarySharesMember_zhn9nowNpdH6" title="Purchase price"><ix:nonFraction name="aert:PurchasePrice" contextRef="From2024-04-012024-04-08_custom_SubscriptionAgreementMember_custom_ClassAOrdinarySharesMember" id="Fact002541" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="INF" unitRef="USDPShares">2.21</ix:nonFraction></span> per share and reserved 320,820 Class A ordinary shares in adherence to the Beneficial Ownership Limitation. On July&#160;10, 2024, and September&#160;25, 2025, the Company issued <span id="xdx_904_eus-gaap--CommonStockSharesIssued_iI_pid_c20240710__us-gaap--TypeOfArrangementAxis__custom--SubscriptionAgreementMember__us-gaap--StatementClassOfStockAxis__custom--ClassAOrdinarySharesMember_zMe3KhNhoXm7" title="Common stock, shares issued"><ix:nonFraction name="us-gaap:CommonStockSharesIssued" contextRef="AsOf2024-07-10_custom_SubscriptionAgreementMember_custom_ClassAOrdinarySharesMember" id="Fact002543" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="INF" unitRef="Shares">270,820</ix:nonFraction></span> and <span id="xdx_906_eus-gaap--CommonStockSharesIssued_iI_pid_c20250925__us-gaap--TypeOfArrangementAxis__custom--SubscriptionAgreementMember__us-gaap--StatementClassOfStockAxis__custom--ClassAOrdinarySharesMember_zIdYAc6VbFf2" title="Common stock, shares issued"><ix:nonFraction name="us-gaap:CommonStockSharesIssued" contextRef="AsOf2025-09-25_custom_SubscriptionAgreementMember_custom_ClassAOrdinarySharesMember" id="Fact002545" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="INF" unitRef="Shares">50,000</ix:nonFraction></span> shares, respectively, from the previously reserved pool of <span id="xdx_90F_eus-gaap--CommonStockCapitalSharesReservedForFutureIssuance_iI_pid_c20240408__us-gaap--TypeOfArrangementAxis__custom--SubscriptionAgreementMember__us-gaap--StatementClassOfStockAxis__custom--ClassAOrdinarySharesMember_zyw1gs4hWjy9" title="Stock reserved"><ix:nonFraction name="us-gaap:CommonStockCapitalSharesReservedForFutureIssuance" contextRef="AsOf2024-04-08_custom_SubscriptionAgreementMember_custom_ClassAOrdinarySharesMember" id="Fact002547" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="INF" unitRef="Shares">320,820</ix:nonFraction></span> shares, resulting in no remaining shares available for issuance.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; text-align: justify; margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0"><b>Exchange Pursuant to Exchange Agreement</b></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; text-align: justify; margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0">Upon consummation of the Business Combination, the holders of AARK ordinary shares and ATGBA ordinary shares each entered into the Exchange Agreements. Pursuant to the Exchange Agreements, from the date of the Exchange Agreements and after April&#160;1, 2024, and subject to certain exercise condition, each shareholder of AARK ordinary shares shall have the right to require the Company to provide Class A ordinary shares or cash in exchange for up to all of the AARK ordinary share. Each share of AARK may be exchanged for 2,246 Class A ordinary shares the Company subject to certain adjustments.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; text-align: justify; margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0">Pursuant to the Exchange Agreements, on April&#160;5, 2024, <span id="xdx_908_ecustom--ExchangeAgreementDescription_c20240401__20240405__us-gaap--TypeOfArrangementAxis__custom--SubscriptionAgreementMember__srt--TitleOfIndividualAxis__custom--AARKMember_zLVwvMkMTEw6" title="Exchange agreement description"><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="From2024-04-012024-04-05_custom_SubscriptionAgreementMember_custom_AARKMember" id="Fact002549" name="aert:ExchangeAgreementDescription">the prior investor of AARK has exchanged 9,500 ordinary shares of AARK for 21,337,000 Class A ordinary shares of the Company (i.e. <span id="xdx_904_eus-gaap--DebtConversionConvertedInstrumentSharesIssued1_pid_c20240401__20240408__us-gaap--TypeOfArrangementAxis__custom--SubscriptionAgreementMember__us-gaap--StatementClassOfStockAxis__custom--ClassAOrdinarySharesMember__srt--TitleOfIndividualAxis__custom--AARKMember_z3cJsDraGqac" title="Share exchanged"><ix:nonFraction name="us-gaap:DebtConversionConvertedInstrumentSharesIssued1" contextRef="From2024-04-012024-04-08_custom_SubscriptionAgreementMember_custom_ClassAOrdinarySharesMember_custom_AARKMember" id="Fact002551" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="INF" unitRef="Shares">2,246</ix:nonFraction></span> Class A ordinary shares of the Company for 1 ordinary share of AARK).</ix:nonNumeric></span></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; text-align: justify; margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0">On September&#160;22, 2025, the Company issued <span id="xdx_902_eus-gaap--StockIssuedDuringPeriodSharesNewIssues_pid_c20250901__20250922_znRBSDOU8ZQ5" title="Shares issued"><ix:nonFraction name="us-gaap:StockIssuedDuringPeriodSharesNewIssues" contextRef="From2025-09-012025-09-22" id="Fact002553" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="INF" unitRef="Shares">851,184</ix:nonFraction></span> shares at a fair value of $<span id="xdx_90A_eus-gaap--SharesIssuedPricePerShare_iI_pid_c20250922_zTLYQ2slFzXf" title="Shares at a fair value"><ix:nonFraction name="us-gaap:SharesIssuedPricePerShare" contextRef="AsOf2025-09-22" id="Fact002555" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="INF" unitRef="USDPShares">0.87</ix:nonFraction></span> per share to Mr. Bhisham (Ajay) Khare pursuant to his Exchange Agreement for shares of ATGBA. As of March&#160;31, 2026, Mr. Bhisham (Ajay) Khare is yet to transfer the shares to the Company and consequently a receivable of $<span id="xdx_909_ecustom--ReceivableRecognized_pn3n3_c20260301__20260331_zEstX29K2fYd" title="Receivable recognized"><ix:nonFraction name="aert:ReceivableRecognized" contextRef="From2026-03-012026-03-31" id="Fact002557" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="-3" scale="3" unitRef="USD">741</ix:nonFraction></span> amount has been recognized.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; text-align: justify; margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0"><b>Shares issued to vendors</b></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; text-align: justify; margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0">In December&#160;2023, ATI settled the amounts owed to certain vendors by issuance of Class A ordinary shares. If the VWAP of the Class A ordinary shares over the three trading days immediately preceding the agreement date is higher than the VWAP over the three trading days immediately preceding the six-month anniversary from the agreement date, ATI would need to issue additional Class A ordinary shares for the difference.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; text-align: justify; margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0">Pursuant to the abovementioned clause, the Company has issued in total <span id="xdx_90E_eus-gaap--StockIssuedDuringPeriodSharesOther_pid_c20240501__20240524__us-gaap--TypeOfArrangementAxis__custom--SubscriptionAgreementMember__srt--TitleOfIndividualAxis__custom--VendorsMember_z4YQJtvSNojb" title="Number of shares issued"><ix:nonFraction name="us-gaap:StockIssuedDuringPeriodSharesOther" contextRef="From2024-05-012024-05-24_custom_SubscriptionAgreementMember_custom_VendorsMember" id="Fact002559" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="INF" unitRef="Shares">54,074</ix:nonFraction></span> Class A ordinary shares to the vendors on May&#160;24, 2024.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; text-align: justify; margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0">In September&#160;2024, the Company issued&#160;<span id="xdx_90F_eus-gaap--StockIssuedDuringPeriodSharesNewIssues_pid_c20240901__20240930__srt--TitleOfIndividualAxis__custom--VendorsMember__us-gaap--StatementClassOfStockAxis__custom--ClassAOrdinarySharesMember_zBp1ZECKdOVj" title="Shares issued"><ix:nonFraction name="us-gaap:StockIssuedDuringPeriodSharesNewIssues" contextRef="From2024-09-012024-09-30_custom_VendorsMember_custom_ClassAOrdinarySharesMember" id="Fact002561" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="INF" unitRef="Shares">78,947</ix:nonFraction></span>&#160;Class A ordinary shares and&#160;<span id="xdx_900_eus-gaap--StockIssuedDuringPeriodSharesNewIssues_pid_c20240901__20240930__srt--TitleOfIndividualAxis__custom--VendorsMember__us-gaap--StatementClassOfStockAxis__custom--ClassVOrdinarySharesMember_ztbeESj8rvW" title="Shares issued"><ix:nonFraction name="us-gaap:StockIssuedDuringPeriodSharesNewIssues" contextRef="From2024-09-012024-09-30_custom_VendorsMember_custom_ClassVOrdinarySharesMember" id="Fact002563" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="INF" unitRef="Shares">48,618</ix:nonFraction></span>&#160;Class A ordinary shares, each valued on the relevant dates of the respective agreements, to two separate vendors, as compensation for their respective services.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; text-align: justify; margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0">In September 2025, the Company, pursuant to a vendor agreement, issued <span id="xdx_902_eus-gaap--StockIssuedDuringPeriodSharesNewIssues_pid_c20250901__20250930__srt--TitleOfIndividualAxis__custom--VendorsMember__us-gaap--StatementClassOfStockAxis__custom--ClassAOrdinarySharesMember_zdZGXzefHnq" title="Shares issued"><ix:nonFraction name="us-gaap:StockIssuedDuringPeriodSharesNewIssues" contextRef="From2025-09-012025-09-30_custom_VendorsMember_custom_ClassAOrdinarySharesMember" id="Fact002565" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="INF" unitRef="Shares">300,000</ix:nonFraction></span> Class A ordinary shares valued on the relevant date of the agreement, as compensation for their services.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; text-align: justify; margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0"><b>Redeemable noncontrolling interest</b></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; text-align: justify; margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0">As of March&#160;31, 2026, the prior investors of AARK owns <span id="xdx_902_eus-gaap--MinorityInterestOwnershipPercentageByNoncontrollingOwners_iI_pid_c20260331__srt--OwnershipAxis__custom--AARKMember_zLUaq77OaNmc" title="Ownership percentage"><ix:nonFraction name="us-gaap:MinorityInterestOwnershipPercentageByNoncontrollingOwners" contextRef="AsOf2026-03-31_custom_AARKMember" id="Fact002570" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="INF" scale="-2" unitRef="Ratio">3.09</ix:nonFraction>%</span> of the ordinary shares of AARK, and prior investors of ATGBA owned <span id="xdx_90C_eus-gaap--MinorityInterestOwnershipPercentageByNoncontrollingOwners_iI_pid_c20260331__srt--OwnershipAxis__custom--ATGBAMember_zdYSZAZsDHe5" title="Ownership percentage"><ix:nonFraction name="us-gaap:MinorityInterestOwnershipPercentageByNoncontrollingOwners" contextRef="AsOf2026-03-31_custom_ATGBAMember" id="Fact002572" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="INF" scale="-2" unitRef="Ratio">17.08</ix:nonFraction>%</span> of the ordinary shares of ATGBA. The prior investors of AARK and ATGBA have the right to exchange their AARK or ATGBA ordinary shares for Class A ordinary shares of the Company based on the exchange ratio as set out in the Exchange Agreements details of which are set out in Note 16 or cash proceeds based on the VWAP for each of the five consecutive trading days ending on the exchange date, but only if the approval from the Reserve Bank of India or other regulatory approvals are not obtained and subject to other conditions specified in the Exchange Agreements. The exchange is also subject to certain other specified conditions being met, including achieving certain financial and stock price milestones. Given that this is not solely in control of ATI, the noncontrolling interests have been accounted for in accordance with ASC 480-10-S99-1. The redeemable noncontrolling interest has initially been measured at the proportionate share in the net assets of AARK and its subsidiaries in accordance with ASC 805-40-30-3. The cash redemption is not considered to be probable on March&#160;31, 2026 because the specified conditions in relation to EBITDA and revenue have already been met and the Reserve Bank of India and / or applicable regulatory approvals are expected to be received. On this basis the redeemable noncontrolling interest has subsequently been measured by attributing the net income/ loss of AARK pursuant to ASC 810-10.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; text-align: justify; margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0">The change in the fair value of the forward purchase agreement put option liability of $<span id="xdx_90E_ecustom--ChangeInFairValueGain_pn3n3_c20250401__20260331__us-gaap--ClassOfWarrantOrRightAxis__custom--ForwardPurchaseAgreementDerivativeLiabilitiesMember_zUnVgbv9qcbl" title="Change in fair value (gain)"><ix:nonFraction name="aert:ChangeInFairValueGain" contextRef="From2025-04-012026-03-31_custom_ForwardPurchaseAgreementDerivativeLiabilitiesMember" id="Fact002648" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="-3" scale="3" unitRef="USD">51</ix:nonFraction></span> has been recorded to change in fair value of forward purchase agreement put option liability for the year ended March&#160;31, 2026 and in the Company&#8217;s consolidated statements of operations. The forward purchase agreement put option liability was classified as a current liability, as its liquidation is reasonably expected to use or require current assets or the creation of current liabilities. See also Notes 2 and 17. The estimated fair value of the forward purchase agreement put option liability was calculated using a Monte Carlo model and used significant assumptions including the risk-free rate and volatility. The change in fair value of the forward purchase agreement put option liability is primarily driven by a decrease in the price per share of the Company.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; text-align: justify; margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0">As of the date of this Form 10-K report, the remaining balance owed to the FPA holders is $<span id="xdx_90D_ecustom--SettlementOfAccountsPayableThroughCashOrInEquity_pn3n3_c20250401__20260331__us-gaap--ClassOfWarrantOrRightAxis__custom--ForwardPurchaseAgreementDerivativeLiabilitiesMember_zfpI0tQcc5tj" title="Settlement of accounts payable through cash or in equity"><ix:nonFraction name="aert:SettlementOfAccountsPayableThroughCashOrInEquity" contextRef="From2025-04-012026-03-31_custom_ForwardPurchaseAgreementDerivativeLiabilitiesMember" id="Fact002650" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="-3" scale="3" unitRef="USD">4,287</ix:nonFraction></span>, which may be settled either in cash or in equity, at the option of the investors.</p>

</ix:nonNumeric><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="From2025-04-01to2026-03-31" escape="true" id="Fact002713" name="us-gaap:EarningsPerShareTextBlock"><p id="xdx_80C_eus-gaap--EarningsPerShareTextBlock_zrZdkmKl2lGg" style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; text-align: justify; margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0"><b>Note 21 - <span id="xdx_822_zu6s2oAcFwAa">Net income / (loss) per Share</span></b></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; text-align: justify; margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0">Basic net income / (loss) per share (&#8220;EPS&#8221;) attributable to Class A ordinary shareholders is calculated by dividing net income / (loss) attributable to Class A ordinary shareholders by the weighted number of Class A ordinary shares outstanding during the reporting period. Diluted EPS is computed using the weighted number of Class A ordinary shares and, when dilutive, potential outstanding shares during the period.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; text-align: justify; margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0">The Company&#8217;s Class V ordinary share does not participate in the earnings or losses of the Company and are therefore not participating securities. As such, separate presentation of basic and diluted net income / (loss) per Class V ordinary share under the two-class method has not been presented.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; text-align: justify; margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0">The following table sets forth the computation of basic and diluted net income / (loss) per share for the year ended March&#160;31, 2026 and March&#160;31, 2025 (in thousands, except share and per share amounts):</p>
